title: Quantum Enhancement Of Information-mediated Energy Transfer
authors: Shotaro Oki, Yuki Kadono, Kaito Tojo, Takahiro Sagawa, Ken Funo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermodynamics of information identifies information flow as a thermodynamic resource, but whether quantum coherence and collective coupling can enhance it at low entropy-production cost remains unresolved. We address this question for interacting open quantum systems by deriving a thermodynamic uncertainty relation that bounds information flow by entropy production in nonequilibrium steady states. We construct a quantum engine in which N-fold degenerate ground and excited states are collectively coupled to heat baths. Collective jumps enhance heat currents and information flow linearly with N, while entropy production remains independent of N, realizing a high-power, low-dissipation autonomous quantum Maxwell's demon that leverages collectively enhanced information flow to pump heat against a temperature gradient. Beyond steady states, collective interactions amplify the unitary component of quantum information flow, yielding a quadratic enhancement of the free-energy charging power of quantum batteries. Our results reveal scalable advantages of quantum coherence and collective effects in quantum engines.
tldr: This paper derives a thermodynamic uncertainty relation linking information flow and entropy production, and demonstrates that collective quantum effects can enhance information-mediated energy transfer with minimal dissipation.
motivation: The authors aim to resolve whether quantum coherence and collective coupling can enhance information flow in thermodynamic processes at low entropy-production cost, which is a key question in quantum thermodynamics.
method: They derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation for interacting open quantum systems in nonequilibrium steady states, and construct a quantum engine with N-fold degenerate states collectively coupled to heat baths.
result: Collective jumps enhance heat currents and information flow linearly with N while entropy production remains independent of N, enabling a high-power, low-dissipation autonomous Maxwell's demon; collective interactions also yield quadratic enhancement of free-energy charging power in quantum batteries.
conclusion: Quantum coherence and collective effects provide scalable advantages in quantum engines, offering a pathway to high-efficiency, low-dissipation information-to-energy conversion.

title: Jarzynski Equality For Counterwork Under Reversed Memory-filtered Driving
authors: Pierre Naz\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a counterwork functional generated by a sign-inverting memory-filtered effective protocol. Given an imposed protocol [MATH], the effective protocol [MATH] is obtained by applying an active protocol-memory kernel to [MATH], rather than by invoking a passive bath response. The counterwork is then the ordinary Hamiltonian work associated with [MATH], so that Jarzynski's equality applies directly to it. When [MATH] reverses the endpoints of [MATH], the corresponding free-energy difference satisfies [MATH], and the exponential average of the counterwork is the reciprocal of that of the original work. We derive the kernel normalization realizing this reversed displacement and show, by Jensen's inequality, that the product of the exponentials of the average work and counterwork is bounded by unity, implying [MATH]. Thus negative average counterwork is possible only when compensated by the average work of the original operation. We further discuss the counteroperation under incomplete thermodynamic information, showing that the robust strategy is to enforce endpoint reversal while minimizing dissipated counterwork.
tldr: The paper introduces a counterwork functional for memory-filtered driving and proves a Jarzynski equality for it, with implications for work extraction under incomplete information.
motivation: To extend fluctuation theorems to non-Markovian driving where the protocol is filtered by a memory kernel, enabling new thermodynamic relations.
method: Defines an effective protocol via a memory kernel, derives the counterwork as ordinary Hamiltonian work under the effective protocol, and uses Jarzynski equality and Jensen's inequality to bound average work.
result: The exponential average of counterwork equals the reciprocal of the original work's exponential average when endpoints are reversed; negative average counterwork requires compensation by positive average work.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust strategy for endpoint reversal while minimizing dissipated counterwork, relevant for thermodynamic processes with memory.

title: No Cloning Of Quantum Ensembles
authors: Zhenyu Du, Siyuan Cheng, Qi Zhao, Xiongfeng Ma, Xiao Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern quantum physics now enables control of quantum systems at the level of individual trajectories, opening a new frontier that links quantum information theory, quantum many-body physics, and quantum thermodynamics, and uncovers novel non-equilibrium phenomena such as deep thermalization and measurement-induced entanglement. However, a central challenge remains: their characterization relies on measuring nonlinear properties of individual quantum states, a task tantamount to fine-grained cloning of a quantum ensemble. Here, the fundamental laws governing the cloning of quantum ensembles are investigated. First, a general no-cloning theorem for arbitrary ensembles is established from an information-theoretic perspective, even assuming multiple copies of the ensemble's purification. It is then shown that this barrier can be unexpectedly circumvented for physical ensembles generated by finite-time evolutions. Nevertheless, these tasks are proven to remain computationally intractable, even when the full circuit description of state preparation is known. This stands in sharp contrast to the conventional no-cloning theorem, which relies on the state being unknown. Together, these results establish new fundamental principles of quantum mechanics, reveal intrinsic trade-offs among sample complexity, computational complexity, and quantum measurements, and highlight the necessity of problem-specific strategies for probing measurement-induced quantum phenomena.
tldr: Establishes a no-cloning theorem for quantum ensembles and shows that while physical ensembles from finite-time evolutions can be cloned, the task remains computationally intractable.
motivation: Characterizing nonlinear properties of individual quantum states is essential for probing modern quantum phenomena but requires fine-grained cloning of ensembles, which is believed to be impossible.
method: The authors prove a general no-cloning theorem for arbitrary ensembles from an information-theoretic perspective, then show that physical ensembles generated by finite-time evolutions can circumvent this barrier, yet prove computational hardness even with full circuit description.
result: A fundamental no-cloning theorem for quantum ensembles is established, with a surprising loophole for physical ensembles that is nonetheless computationally intractable.
conclusion: The results reveal intrinsic trade-offs among sample complexity, computational complexity, and quantum measurements, highlighting the need for problem-specific strategies in probing measurement-induced quantum phenomena.

title: Industry-ready Spin-photon Interfaces For Hybrid Photonic Quantum Computing
authors: H\^elio Huet, Hubert Lam, Thibaut Pollet, Petr Steindl, Alice Bernard, Albert Adiyatullin, Petr Stepanov, William Hease, Victor Guilloux, Nico Margaria, Joris Verstraten, Raksha Singla, Samuel T. abstract: ArXiv:2606.27787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid photonic quantum computers, combining stationary matter qubits and flying photonic qubits, offer an intrinsically networked and resource-efficient route to large-scale, error-corrected quantum computation. Their core components are cavity-coupled matter qubits that act as light--matter interfaces, enabling: high-efficiency on-demand single-photon generation, stable near-unity photon indistinguishability and spin--multi-photon entanglement. Semiconductor quantum dots in microcavities are a leading platform for realizing such devices. Yet reaching the performance, reproducibility and spin-coherence thresholds for large-scale error correction remains a major challenge requiring industrial fabrication and control. Here we report thousands of monolithic semiconductor quantum-dot devices fabricated using a III--V pilot production-line process compatible with large-scale deployment. Systematic control of source parameters yields state-of-the-art efficiency and supports a path to optical losses below fault-tolerance thresholds. Using field-quadrature state reconstruction as a stringent joint test of efficiency and indistinguishability, we observe near-unity photon quantum purity stable over tens of minutes and a record single-photon Wigner-function negativity. We further demonstrate seven-partite spin--multi-photon entanglement and spin coherence extendable to microsecond timescales in the low-magnetic-field regime. Finally, photons from distant sources are as indistinguishable as photons emitted successively by a single source. These results establish foundry-compatible III--V quantum dots as a scalable platform for hybrid photonic quantum computing.
tldr: This paper demonstrates industry-ready spin-photon interfaces using semiconductor quantum dots in microcavities, achieving high-efficiency single-photon generation, near-unity indistinguishability, and multi-partite entanglement, paving the way for scalable hybrid photonic quantum computing.
motivation: Hybrid photonic quantum computers require high-performance, reproducible light-matter interfaces. Semiconductor quantum dots are promising but need industrial fabrication to meet fault-tolerance thresholds for large-scale error correction.
method: The authors fabricate thousands of monolithic quantum-dot devices using a III-V pilot production-line process. They characterize performance via field-quadrature state reconstruction, measure photon purity and Wigner negativity, demonstrate spin-multi-photon entanglement, and test indistinguishability of photons from distant sources.
result: They achieve state-of-the-art efficiency, near-unity photon quantum purity stable over tens of minutes, a record single-photon Wigner-function negativity, seven-partite spin-multi-photon entanglement, and microsecond spin coherence. Photons from distant sources are as indistinguishable as from a single source.
conclusion: Foundry-compatible III-V quantum dots are a scalable platform for hybrid photonic quantum computing, meeting key performance metrics for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Single-sideband-interference Twin-field Quantum Key Distribution Without Global Phase Locking
authors: Xingjian Li, Bingkun Wang, Jianyong Hu, Jianqiang Liu, Shuxiao Wu, Guosheng Feng, Zhixing Qiao, Changgang Yang, Ruiyun Chen, Chengbing Qin, Guofeng Zhang, Liantuan Xiao, Suotang Jia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twin-field quantum key distribution (TF QKD) can overcome the fundamental rate loss limit of repeaterless quantum links, but its practical deployment has long been hindered by the requirement of global phase locking between two independent lasers. By revisiting the fundamental principles of optical interference, this work reveals that interference in TF QKD inherently relies only on the instantaneous phase alignment of two independent optical pulses at the moment they temporally overlap, rather than on continuous global phase synchronization. Guided by this insight, we propose and demonstrate a single-sideband-interference TF-QKD protocol that eliminates global phase locking. Each user employs an IQ modulator to generate a weak single sideband as the quantum signal, while the intrinsically phase-correlated optical carrier propagates as a real-time phase reference. Carrier interference at the receiver enables real-time phase extraction and feedback compensation for the sidebands. Unlike prior no phase locking approaches requiring second- or microsecond-level coherence, in principle, our scheme reduces this requirement to nanoseconds. We achieve 98% interference visibility over 100.8 km fibre and secure key rates surpassing the PLOB bound in the high-loss regime, providing a simpler route towards practical long-distance quantum communication networks.
tldr: A twin-field QKD protocol that eliminates global phase locking by using single-sideband interference with a real-time phase reference.
motivation: Twin-field QKD can overcome the repeaterless rate limit but requires global phase locking, which hinders practical deployment. This work aims to remove that requirement.
method: Each user generates a weak single sideband as the quantum signal and uses the intrinsically phase-correlated optical carrier as a real-time phase reference; carrier interference at the receiver enables phase extraction and feedback compensation.
result: Achieved 98% interference visibility over 100.8 km fiber and secure key rates surpassing the PLOB bound in the high-loss regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme reduces coherence requirements to nanoseconds, providing a simpler route towards practical long-distance quantum communication networks.

title: Non-equilibrium Quantum Thermometry With Bosonic Samples
authors: Marek Winczewski, Micha{\l} Horodecki, Ricard Ravell Rodr\'iguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study low-temperature non-equilibrium quantum thermometry with a bosonic probe: a quantum harmonic oscillator strongly coupled to a bosonic bath at temperature [MATH] through a Drude--Ohmic spectral density. We treat the probe--bath dynamics both exactly, using the quadratic solution of Boyanovsky and Jasnow, and within a renormalized Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation. From the time-dependent covariance matrix we extract the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for general single-mode Gaussian probe states, including squeezed ones. In the strong-coupling, non-Markovian regime the QFI is non-monotonic in time, displaying bath-memory revivals that make a finite interrogation time [MATH] strictly optimal. By contrast, we prove that the Markovian QFI rises monotonically to its stationary value and develops no interior optimum, so that its optimum is always pinned to the boundary [MATH]; this complements existing Markovian precision-rate bounds, which concern [MATH] rather than the single-shot QFI [MATH]. Squeezed initial states yield a large transient advantage that thermalisation eventually erases, establishing squeezing and interrogation time as complementary thermometric resources. At equilibrium, strong coupling replaces the exponential Boltzmann suppression of the low-temperature relative error by a far milder polynomial divergence. As the model maps directly onto circuit quantum electrodynamics, these protocols appear within current experimental reach.
tldr: This paper studies non-equilibrium quantum thermometry using a bosonic probe strongly coupled to a bath, revealing non-monotonic quantum Fisher information and optimal interrogation times in the non-Markovian regime.
motivation: Accurate low-temperature thermometry is crucial for quantum technologies, but standard probes suffer from exponential suppression of precision at low temperatures. The authors aim to exploit strong coupling and non-Markovian effects to overcome this limitation.
method: They model a quantum harmonic oscillator probe coupled to a bosonic bath via Drude-Ohmic spectral density, solving the dynamics exactly using quadratic solutions and a renormalized GKLS master equation. The quantum Fisher information is computed from the time-dependent covariance matrix for general Gaussian states.
result: In the strong-coupling non-Markovian regime, the QFI is non-monotonic with revivals, leading to a finite optimal interrogation time. Squeezed initial states provide a transient advantage. At equilibrium, strong coupling replaces exponential Boltzmann suppression with a milder polynomial divergence.
conclusion: Strong coupling and non-Markovianity are beneficial resources for low-temperature quantum thermometry, and the protocols are experimentally feasible in circuit QED platforms.

title: A Quantum Method Of Types
authors: Arick Grootveld
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The method of types is a fundamental tool in classical information theory, with applications ranging from composite hypothesis testing and universal source coding to the capacity of arbitrarily varying channels. In this work we introduce an empirical operator acting as a quantum analog of the empirical distribution. We show that this empirical operator satisfies combinatorial and large-deviation bounds, which in combination describe a quantum method of types. As an application, we use this quantum method of types to prove a universal achievability result for composite quantum hypothesis testing.
tldr: Introduces a quantum analog of the method of types using an empirical operator, with applications to composite quantum hypothesis testing.
motivation: The classical method of types is a powerful tool in information theory, but a quantum generalization has been lacking. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Defines an empirical operator as the quantum analog of the empirical distribution, and proves combinatorial and large-deviation bounds for it.
result: Establishes a quantum method of types and uses it to prove a universal achievability result for composite quantum hypothesis testing.
conclusion: The quantum method of types provides a new framework for analyzing quantum information-theoretic problems, with potential applications beyond hypothesis testing.

title: Scalable Acceleration Of Many-Body Quantum Dynamics Via Time-Rescaling
authors: Edson B. de Almeida Filho, \^angelo F. Da Silva Fran\c{c}a, Bert\'ulio de Lima Bernardo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast quantum control is essential to overcome decoherence in contemporary quantum platforms, yet achieving this in many-body systems remains a major challenge. We show that the time-rescaling (TR) method enables efficient acceleration of closed many-body quantum dynamics, extending its applicability beyond previously studied regimes. Applying TR to the transverse-field Ising model with a longitudinal field, we demonstrate a significant enhancement of quantum annealing performance, maintaining high ground-state fidelity at evolution times where standard adiabatic dynamics breaks down, with only weak dependence on system size. We further demonstrate high-fidelity preparation of Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states in many-body systems, where TR extends the accessible system sizes within fixed evolution times. We additionally show that the Mandelstam-Tamm quantum speed limit does not fundamentally limit the acceleration achievable through TR, as the reduction in evolution time is exactly compensated by increased energy fluctuations. These results establish TR as a scalable and experimentally viable approach to fast quantum control in many-body systems.
tldr: The paper shows that time-rescaling (TR) method accelerates many-body quantum dynamics, enhancing quantum annealing and GHZ state preparation while circumventing the Mandelstam-Tamm speed limit.
motivation: Fast quantum control is needed to overcome decoherence, but accelerating many-body dynamics is challenging. The authors aim to extend the TR method to many-body systems.
method: They apply the TR method to the transverse-field Ising model with a longitudinal field, analyzing quantum annealing performance and GHZ state preparation via numerical simulations.
result: TR significantly improves ground-state fidelity in quantum annealing with weak system-size dependence, enables high-fidelity GHZ state preparation for larger systems, and shows that the quantum speed limit is not a fundamental barrier.
conclusion: TR is a scalable and experimentally viable approach for fast quantum control in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Memory And Thermal Amplification In Spin--cavity Squared Commutators
authors: Yong-Hong Ma, Hui-Hui Xu, Jian-Zhuang Wu, Quan-Zhen Ding, Wu-Ming Liu, Xin-Yu Zhao, E Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Squared commutators in the Holstein--Primakoff limit of a spin--cavity system provide a compact way to separate propagation from covariance growth in a finite-temperature reservoir with memory. In the finite-temperature NMQSD construction, the linear quadrature commutator is fixed by the retarded spin--cavity propagator, whereas a quadratic commutator carries the same retarded factor together with a covariance factor. For a zero-mean Gaussian state, \(C_{R_i^2,R_j}(t)=4|\kappa_{ij}(t)|^2V_{ii}(t)\); the symmetrized expression gives the spin-side and mixed channels. Since \(\bar n\) enters the covariance sector but not the homogeneous retarded kernel, raising \(\bar n\) from 0 to 1 leaves the linear transfer unchanged while increasing the quadratic signal. Varying the bath-memory rate and the counter-rotating coupling within the stable HP region then shows how stored cavity history changes both the transfer weight and its distribution in time. The calculation separates memory-dependent propagation from thermal covariance growth in collective spin--cavity dynamics.
tldr: This paper analyzes memory and thermal amplification in a spin-cavity system using squared commutators within the Holstein-Primakoff limit.
motivation: Understanding how finite-temperature reservoirs with memory affect quantum dynamics is crucial for hybrid quantum systems, particularly spin ensembles coupled to cavities.
method: The authors employ the finite-temperature NMQSD (Non-Markovian Quantum State Diffusion) formalism to separate memory-dependent propagation from thermal covariance growth, deriving expressions for linear and quadratic commutators.
result: They find that increasing the thermal photon number enhances the quadratic signal without affecting linear transfer, and that bath-memory rate and counter-rotating coupling modulate the transfer weight and its temporal distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a compact framework to analyze memory effects and thermal noise in spin-cavity systems, relevant for quantum information processing with hybrid platforms.

title: Factorization Through Lorentz Cones
authors: Guillaume Aubrun, Francesca la Piana, Alexander M\"uller-Hermes

Clearly, [MATH] has the LFP if either [MATH] or [MATH] is a direct sum of Lorentzian cones, and our main goal is to find other examples. We show that such examples cannot be found for pairs [MATH] where [MATH], or in the case where both [MATH] and [MATH] are polyhedral. Here, we show that [MATH] has the LFP whenever [MATH] is a symmetric cone, i.e., a direct sum of Lorentz cones, cones of positive semidefinite matrices over the real numbers, complex numbers or quaternions, and the cone of [MATH] positive semidefinite matrices over the octonions. tldr: This paper studies the Lorentz factorization property for proper cones and applies it to a problem in quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding when positive maps factor through Lorentzian cones is a structural question with implications for quantum information, particularly in the study of entanglement and positive maps.
method: The authors define the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) and characterize pairs of cones that satisfy it, using convex geometry and cone theory. They prove impossibility results for certain cone dimensions and polyhedral cones, and show that symmetric cones have LFP when paired with a square-based cone.
result: The paper provides a complete characterization for certain cone pairs, showing that LFP holds for symmetric cones with a square-based cone, and fails for many other cases. An application to quantum information is discussed.
conclusion: The Lorentz factorization property is a new structural concept that connects convex geometry to quantum information, and the results suggest further open questions about its scope.

A pair (C1, C2) has the LFP if every positive map from C1 to C2 factors through a direct sum of Lorentzian cones (cones over Euclidean balls). The authors aim to find non-trivial examples beyond the obvious case where one cone is itself a direct sum of Lorentzian cones. The paper concludes with an application to quantum information theory, specifically to the problem of characterizing cones that allow for a certain type of entanglement detection.

title: Verifiable And Collusion-Resistant Multi-Party Quantum Private Set Operations
authors: Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Fengxia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threshold private set intersection (TPSI) allows parties to reveal their intersection only when its cardinality reaches a prescribed threshold. Existing quantum TPSI protocols typically rely on a third party (TP) to interpret the final results, which deviates from the cardinality-testing paradigm of TPSI. In this paper, we propose a quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing. Our protocol develops a rotation-based quantum construction in which single-photon sequences are sequentially processed through participant-side data rotations, TP--participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors: TP can complete the final measurement, but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of the outcomes. Based on these hidden measurements, we further realize the threshold decision through an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only \(\mathbf 1[|\bigcap_i X_i|\ge \tau]\) before conditional intersection reconstruction. We prove the correctness and security of the proposed protocol, and further validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations implemented on the IBM platform.

title: Composing Quantum Instruments
authors: Robert I. Booth, Dominik Leichtle, Alex Rice, Kim Worrall
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the composition of classically-controlled quantum instruments--the natural quantum analogue of Markov kernels. Classically, Markov kernels compose by integrating one kernel against another. Defining this composition for quantum instruments with continuous outcomes requires an integral of quantum channel-valued functions with respect to a quantum instrument. We construct this integral in the Heisenberg picture using the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension to a von Neumann tensor product. This integral recovers the expected finite formula, preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality, and provides the multiplication for a monad governing the composition of quantum instruments. As an immediate consequence, we identify the category of quantum Markov kernels as the Kleisli category of this monad.

conclusion: This work provides a foundational categorical framework for composing quantum instruments, which is essential for understanding sequential quantum processes and quantum information flow.

title: Engineering Of non-Hermitian Interactions In Digital Qudit Quantum Simulators
authors: Matteo M. Wauters, Paolo Boschetto, Edoardo Ballini, Alberto Biella, Philipp Hauke
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians are a fascinating class of many-body models that describe the effective dynamics of quantum systems interacting with the environment through particle, energy, or information exchange. Although their theoretical framework is well established, the controlled engineering of such Hamiltonians in the context of quantum simulations remains challenging, even more so when the non-Hermitian part describes a [MATH]-body interaction. Qudit quantum simulators offer a compelling framework to implement such models. We theoretically investigate the dynamics of a one-dimensional chain of qudits undergoing hybrid unitary-projective evolution, where suitably designed measurements constrain the dynamics to a Zeno subspace. As we illustrate for the case of qutrits, within the Zeno subspace the dynamics is governed by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for an ensemble of pseudo-spins [MATH], which can inherit non-Hermitian two-body interactions with the same connectivity as the full qutrit chain. We derive an analytical relation linking the monitored qutrits' evolution to a desired target non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and validate the effective description through numerical simulations of a representative model. Our scheme provides a constructive route for the realization of a large class of interacting non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians in experimentally relevant multilevel quantum platforms, including trapped ions and superconducting circuits.

title: Enhancing Quantum Metrology With High-order Fisher Information And Experiments
authors: Xin-Zhu Liu, Jun-Li Jiang, Yan-Han Yang, Li-Ming Zhao, Xue Yang, Shao-Ming Fei, Ming-Xing Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fisher information plays a central role in statistics and quantum metrology, providing the basis for the celebrated Cram\'{e}r-Rao bound. In this work, we introduce a new information measure based on higher-order Fisher information and show that it naturally leads to a generalized uncertainty relation for parameter estimation, which can be regarded as an extension of the Cram\'er-Rao bound. As an application, we analyze the case of quantum phase estimation with a single qubit and compare our theoretical bounds with the well-known established hierarchical bounds. Finally, we experimentally validate the proposed framework using a photonic platform.
tldr: Introduces a new information measure based on higher-order Fisher information, leading to a generalized uncertainty relation for parameter estimation, and experimentally validates it with a photonic platform.
motivation: Fisher information is central to quantum metrology, but standard Cramér-Rao bounds may not capture all information; higher-order Fisher information can provide tighter bounds.
method: Defines higher-order Fisher information and derives a generalized uncertainty relation; applies to quantum phase estimation with a single qubit and compares with hierarchical bounds; experimental validation on a photonic platform.
result: The new measure yields tighter bounds than standard Cramér-Rao bounds, and experimental results confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Higher-order Fisher information offers a more complete framework for parameter estimation, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Standard-quantum-limit-surpassing Vector Polarimetry Using Rydberg Atoms In An Su(1,1) Interferometer
authors: Weiqiang Guan, Yuetao Chen, Jun Zhou, Keyi Li, Yu Huang, Shaoyan Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector polarimetry is an important application frontier for Rydberg-atom-based sensing. While prior research has largely concentrated on developing novel measurement schemes, high-sensitivity vector polarimetry remains an open question. Here we propose a theoretical framework for high-sensitivity detection of radio-frequency (RF) electric field polarization direction, which is particularly suitable for weak-field detection. Under a static magnetic field, the asymmetry in coupling between the Zeeman sublevels of the Rydberg atom and the RF field's polarization components enables the polarization angles to be determined from the atomic absorption index, which is retrieved via homodyne detection by incorporating the Rydberg atom system into an SU(1,1) interferometer. We derive the sensitivity of the polarization angles along with the corresponding standard quantum limit (SQL) and quantum Cram\'{e}r--Rao bound (QCRB). Our results demonstrate a sensitivity surpassing the SQL across wide angular ranges using either dual coherent states or a coherent state combined with a squeezed vacuum state as input. Significantly, the optimal sensitivity reaches below {\degree}, with sensitivities better than {\degree} maintained over most of the angular domain. This work establishes a foundation for high-precision vector polarimetry, thereby advancing the development of Rydberg-atom-based quantum sensing and contributing to a deeper understanding of light--matter interactions.
tldr: Proposes a high-sensitivity vector polarimetry scheme using Rydberg atoms in an SU(1,1) interferometer, surpassing the standard quantum limit.
motivation: High-sensitivity vector polarimetry for RF electric fields is challenging; prior work focused on novel schemes but not sensitivity limits.
method: Rydberg atoms in a static magnetic field couple Zeeman sublevels to RF polarization; homodyne detection via SU(1,1) interferometer retrieves polarization angles; sensitivity derived via SQL and QCRB.
result: Sensitivity surpasses SQL over wide angular ranges using dual coherent states or coherent+squeezed vacuum; optimal sensitivity below 0.1°.
conclusion: Establishes foundation for high-precision vector polarimetry, advancing Rydberg-atom quantum sensing and light-matter interaction understanding.

title: Photon Avalanche Triggered By A Single Photon In A Bistable Nonlinear Optical Cavity
authors: Asian Selvakumaran, Anna Minguzzi, Iacopo Carusotto, Maxime Richard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the response of a coherently-driven nonlinear optical cavity to an additional incident single photon. Using a quantum description of the nonlinear dynamics that fully accounts for the quantum fluctuations of the cavity field and for the discrete nature of the incident photon, we characterize the quantum dynamics of single-photon-stimulated jumps from the low-photon-number to the high-photon-number state of the optical bistability loop. We find that the system can exhibit a giant response to this single quantum of excitation, rooted in the phase-transition picture of optical bistability. In addition to shedding light on the role of quantum fluctuations in the non-equilibrium dynamics of a nonlinear optical cavity, our results suggest a strategy for an all-optical single-photon avalanche detector.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates that a single photon can trigger a macroscopic avalanche in a bistable nonlinear optical cavity, enabling an all-optical single-photon detector.
motivation: To explore the quantum dynamics of photon-triggered switching in optical bistability and propose a novel single-photon detection mechanism.
method: A quantum description of the nonlinear cavity dynamics is used, accounting for quantum fluctuations and the discrete nature of the incident photon, to simulate the stimulated jump from low to high photon number.
result: The system exhibits a giant response to a single photon, with the switching probability and speed characterized, showing potential for high-sensitivity detection.
conclusion: The results provide insight into non-equilibrium quantum fluctuations and suggest a strategy for an all-optical single-photon avalanche detector.

title: On The Generic Structures Of The Protocols For Quantum Auction And Quantum Summation And Their Relation
authors: Kabir Sandhu, Sandeep Mishra, Anirban Pathak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure multi-party computation (SMC) addresses the problem of jointly computing global functions of private inputs while revealing minimal information about individual data. Two prominent examples of SMC tasks are sealed-bid auction and secure multi-party summation. Existing schemes for quantum auction and quantum summation have largely been developed independently, motivated by distinct applications and employing different computational primitives. In this work, structural symmetries in existing protocols for quantum auction and quantum summation are identified. In particular, it is established that the core auction primitives including revenue estimation, maximum bid identification, and winner determination can be reduced to repeated invocations of a summation oracle acting on suitably defined indicator functions. Conversely, summation protocols can be naturally embedded as auxiliary subroutines within auction frameworks, establishing summation as a unifying primitive underlying a broad class of auction mechanisms. Further, computational, communication and memory costs of these reductions are analyzed and compared with some of the representative existing protocols. The analysis has revealed that the process of implementing summation tasks through currently known auction protocols leads to additional overhead associated with bid-space exploration and winner determination. The proposed framework is protocol-agnostic and applicable across diverse computational models, including gate-based and photonic implementations. Finally, a proof-of-concept experimental realization (numerical validation) of a two-bidder sealed-bid auction using IBM (optical quantum) hardware is demonstrated to establish that the claimed equivalence is not merely formal but experimentally verifiable with the available hardware.
tldr: This paper identifies structural symmetries between quantum auction and quantum summation protocols, showing that auction primitives can be reduced to summation oracles and vice versa.
motivation: Quantum auction and quantum summation protocols have been developed independently; understanding their relationship can unify design and reduce overhead.
method: The authors formally prove that auction tasks (revenue estimation, winner determination) reduce to repeated summation oracles, and embed summation as a subroutine in auctions; they analyze computational, communication, and memory costs.
result: Summation is established as a unifying primitive for quantum auctions; implementing auction via summation incurs additional overhead from bid-space exploration and winner determination.
conclusion: The framework is protocol-agnostic and validated numerically on IBM and optical quantum hardware, confirming the equivalence is experimentally verifiable.

title: Simulating The Dynamics Of Markovian Quantum Processes By Quantum Collision Models On Quantum Computers
authors: Zeqing Wang, Julian D. Teske, Anshuman Bhardwaj, Masahiro O. Takahashi, Seiji Yunoki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamiltonian dynamics have been widely implemented on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices in recent years. In contrast, experimental demonstrations of Markovian quantum dynamics remain limited, because implementing nonunitary evolution on quantum computers is challenging. Quantum collision models provide a natural approach to this problem by coupling the system to ancillas to realize dissipation. However, previous implementations of quantum collision models on quantum computers have typically been restricted to one or two system qubits and fewer than 12 time steps, owing to noise, circuit depth, the overhead of ancilla reset, and limited qubit resources. In this work, we experimentally simulate Markovian quantum processes with local and nonlocal dissipation on both trapped-ion and superconducting quantum computers. By employing hardware-specific ancilla strategies, we realize simulations with up to seven system qubits, corresponding to 13 qubits in total, and 40 time steps. Our results demonstrate that, even for the same physical model, the optimal implementation strategy depends strongly on the hardware characteristics of the quantum computer.
tldr: This paper experimentally simulates Markovian quantum processes using quantum collision models on trapped-ion and superconducting quantum computers, scaling to 7 system qubits and 40 time steps.
motivation: Implementing nonunitary evolution on quantum computers is challenging, and previous collision model simulations were limited to small systems and few time steps due to noise and resource constraints.
method: The authors employ quantum collision models with hardware-specific ancilla strategies to realize local and nonlocal dissipation on both trapped-ion and superconducting platforms.
result: They achieve simulations with up to 7 system qubits (13 total qubits) and 40 time steps, demonstrating that optimal implementation depends on hardware characteristics.
conclusion: The work shows that quantum collision models can be scaled to larger systems on current quantum hardware, with strategies tailored to the specific platform.

title: Quantum Frequency Comb With Pump-selectable Bin Pairing And Extraction-aware Loading In A Lithium Niobate Microresonator
authors: Mohamad Reza Nurrahman (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hyeon Hwang (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Nuri Han (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Guhwan Kim (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hong-Seok Kim (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Kiwon Moon (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Jung Jin Ju (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hansuek Lee (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Min-Kyo Seo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated quantum photonics requires bright, high-fidelity photon-pair sources capable of spectral multiplexing, correlation control, and circuit-compatible extraction. Cavity-enhanced spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enhances pair generation, but triply resonant operation imposes stringent pump-signal-idler spectral-alignment constraints. Moreover, the trade-off between intrinsic generation and coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) does not capture the usable output flux, which depends on photon extraction. Here, we demonstrate a single-pass-pumped, resonator-enhanced quantum frequency comb (QFC) source based on a periodically poled lithium niobate photonic-crystal Fabry-P[MATH]rot microresonator. The device yields intrinsic and loaded brightnesses of 69.9 and 1.88 MHz/[MATH]W, respectively, and a maximum CAR of 16,000. Frequency-resolved measurements reveal 461 cavity-defined bins spanning 1495-1570 nm, and loaded spectral brightness approaching 4.29[MATH]10[MATH] pairs/(s[MATH]mW[MATH]nm). In particular, tuning the single-pass pump deterministically selects correlated frequency-bin pairings within the fixed QFC grid while preserving brightness and pairwise coincidence rates. We further separate intrinsic generation from output photon-pair flux, revealing the loaded-brightness-CAR relation. Together, pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading point to tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light resources for multiphoton-interference quantum simulation and programmable frequency-bin quantum information processing.

conclusion: Pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading enable tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light sources for multiphoton-interference quantum simulation and programmable frequency-bin quantum information processing.

title: Squeezing Enhanced Homodyne Weak Force Sensing In Cavity Optomechanics
authors: Madan Mohan Mahana, Sanket Das, Tarak Nath Dey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cavity optomechanical systems have emerged as a promising platform for quantum sensing. Quantum mechanics imposes a standard quantum limit (SQL) on the force-sensitivity for the standard homodyne phase quadrature measurement of the cavity's output field. In this paper, we investigate ways to enhance sensitivity beyond SQL for weak-force measurement by adopting a variational homodyne quadrature readout and quantum squeezing. Our study reveals a remarkable improvement in the force sensitivity of a cavity optomechanical sensor at a suitable homodyne angle, compared with standard phase quadrature detection of the cavity output field within a specific frequency band. We show that the force sensitivity can be further improved by intra-cavity squeezing (ICS) or injected external squeezing (IES) of the cavity mode. Both variational homodyne readout and quantum squeezing induce quantum correlation between the amplitude and phase quadratures of the cavity's output field, thereby improving the force sensitivity. The squeezing-enhanced variational homodyne detection scheme can enable high-precision sensing across various hybrid quantum platforms.

conclusion: Squeezing-enhanced variational homodyne detection enables high-precision sensing applicable to various hybrid quantum platforms.

title: The Quantum Instrument Monad
authors: Tobias Fritz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monads are a ubiquitous structure in functional programming used for modelling computational effects. For example, the state monad models the effect of a computation interacting with a memory system. Here we introduce the quantum instrument monad [MATH], which models the effect of a computation interacting with a quantum system with algebra of observables [MATH]. It can be thought of as a noncommutative generalization of the state monad. We construct this quantum instrument monad in two versions: a finitary version on the category of sets and a measure-theoretic version on the category of measurable spaces (the latter under the assumption that [MATH] is a type I von Neumann algebra with separable predual). Both versions are strong monads. The construction of the measure-theoretic version is based on a new notion of integral of a quantum-operation-valued function against a state-valued measure.

conclusion: The quantum instrument monad offers a novel categorical tool for quantum information theory, potentially useful for modeling quantum protocols and resources.

title: Quantum Multi-Party Threshold Private Set Intersection With Explicit Cardinality Testing
authors: Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Fengxia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threshold private set intersection (TPSI) allows parties to reveal their intersection only when its cardinality reaches a prescribed threshold. Existing quantum TPSI protocols typically rely on a third party (TP) to interpret the final results, which deviates from the cardinality-testing paradigm of TPSI. In this paper, we propose a quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing. Our protocol develops a rotation-based quantum construction in which single-photon sequences are sequentially processed through participant-side data rotations, TP--participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors: TP can complete the final measurement, but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of the outcomes. Based on these hidden measurements, we further realize the threshold decision through an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only \(\mathbf 1[|\bigcap_i X_i|\ge \tau]\) before conditional intersection reconstruction. We prove the correctness and security of the proposed protocol, and further validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations implemented on the IBM platform.
tldr: A quantum multi-party threshold private set intersection protocol with explicit cardinality testing using rotation-based quantum operations and oblivious linear evaluation.
motivation: Existing quantum TPSI protocols rely on a third party to interpret results, deviating from the cardinality-testing paradigm; a protocol with explicit threshold testing is needed.
method: The protocol uses single-photon sequences with participant-side data rotations, TP-masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations to produce hidden-label measurement vectors, then employs OLE-based inner product and garbled circuits for threshold decision.
result: The protocol is proven correct and secure, and its feasibility is validated via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM's platform.
conclusion: The work provides a quantum multi-party TPSI protocol that achieves explicit cardinality testing without revealing the intersection size, advancing secure multi-party quantum communication.
